intro: Body parts, common injury expressions and the words people use to describe an accident.
p.caerse.nota: Present: me caigo. Preterite: me caí.
p.darse un golpe: to hit or bang a body part
p.la tirita.nota: A small adhesive dressing; the DLE marks tirita as used in Spain. Other varieties use terms such as curita or apósito.
p.torcerse.nota: In the present, o changes to ue (me tuerzo el tobillo); in the preterite it returns to o (me torcí el tobillo).
p.el dedo.nota: In this lesson it means finger; dedo can refer to a finger or toe.
p.el yeso.nota: A synonym of escayola for the cast used to immobilize an injured body part.
b1.texto:
Many common injury expressions use a pronominal verb and a pronoun for the affected person. The body part often takes the definite article rather than a possessive: **me he roto el brazo**, **me he cortado el dedo**, **me quemé la mano**, **me torcí el tobillo**, **me di un golpe en la cabeza**. The pronoun already identifies who is affected. An indefinite article is also possible when introducing an unspecified injury: **me he roto una pierna**.

**Caerse** means to fall: **me caí** por la escalera; **se cayó** de la bici.

A story can set the scene with the imperfect and then report the accident: **estaba cocinando y me quemé**; **iba** en bici y **me caí**.

Possible injuries include **una herida**, **un corte**, **una quemadura** and **un golpe**. For care, you may hear **una tirita**, **una venda**, **hielo**, **una escayola / un yeso**; someone may **ponerte una escayola** or **darte puntos**. **Tirita** is marked as Spanish in the DLE; **curita** and **apósito** are also used.

To ask what happened or how someone feels: **¿Qué te ha pasado?**, **¿Te has hecho daño?**, **¿Te duele?**
b2.f1: I've broken it. I was on my bike, I fell and I banged my elbow.
b2.f2: That sounds painful! Did they put you in a cast?
b2.f3: Yes, for a month. And I sprained my ankle.
b2.f4: Well, yesterday I cut my finger while cooking.
b2.f5: Good thing you only need an adhesive bandage.
b4.pregunta: Complete the exact phrase from the lesson title.
b4.o0.refuerzo: This is the phrase used in the title.
b4.o2.refuerzo: In this pattern, use the article, not a possessive.
b5.pregunta: Complete: I fell down the stairs.
b6.pregunta: What do you put on a small cut?
b6.o0.refuerzo: A small adhesive dressing for a small cut.
b6.o1.refuerzo: A cast immobilizes an injured body part; the question asks about a small cut.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I was cooking when I burned my hand.
b7.o0.refuerzo: The completed accident is expressed with the preterite.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That would describe an ongoing or repeated action.
b8.o1.explicacion: Tobillo is the ankle and torcerse is to sprain.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about an accident, yours or someone else's: what happened and what the consequences were.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Explain aloud to a doctor how you hurt yourself.
b8.o0.explicacion: Me torcí el tobillo means I twisted my ankle, and tobillo is the ankle.
